claim: S3 website endpoints do not support HTTPS or access points; AWS names Amazon CloudFront in front of the bucket as a way to serve the static website over HTTPS.

values.display: do not support HTTPS or access points
Use Amazon CloudFront

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 website endpoints do not support HTTPS or access points.
Use Amazon CloudFront to serve a static website hosted on Amazon S3.

claim: A bucket configured as a static website is served at the Region-specific website endpoint of the bucket, which is different from the REST API endpoint.
question: Where is an S3 static website served, and is that the same endpoint as the S3 REST API?

values.display: AWS Region-specific website endpoint of the bucket
different from the endpoints where you send REST API requests

evidence.quote: When you configure your bucket as a static website, the website is available at the AWS Region-specific website endpoint of the bucket. Website endpoints are different from the endpoints where you send REST API requests.

claim: For a public website on the S3 website endpoint, all content must be publicly readable; the website endpoint supports only publicly readable content.
question: What must be true of the objects for visitors to reach them at an S3 website endpoint?

values.display: make all your content publicly readable

evidence.quote: If you want your website to be public, you must make all your content publicly readable for your customers to be able to access it at the website endpoint.

claim: Requester Pays buckets do not allow access through a website endpoint; any such request receives a 403 Access Denied response.
question: Can a Requester Pays bucket be read through an S3 website endpoint?

values.display: 403 Access Denied
do not allow access through a website endpoint

evidence.quote: Requester Pays buckets do not allow access through a website endpoint. Any request to such a bucket receives a 403 Access Denied response.

claim: A static website bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS must be served through a CloudFront distribution, because SSE-KMS does not support anonymous users; the distribution must use origin access control (OAC), since OAI does not support SSE-KMS.
question: How do you serve a static website from an S3 bucket encrypted with SSE-KMS?

values.display: SSE-KMS doesn't support anonymous users
you must use OAC instead

evidence.quote: If the bucket that you're using to host your static website has been encrypted using server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys (SSE-KMS), you must create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve your website because SSE-KMS doesn't support anonymous users.
OAI doesn't support SSE-KMS, so you must use OAC instead.

claim: Concurrent connections can fetch different byte ranges of the same object, which gives higher aggregate throughput than one whole-object request and shortens retries when a request is interrupted.
question: How do byte-range fetches improve download throughput from S3?

values.display: fetch different byte ranges from within the same object
higher aggregate throughput
improve retry times

evidence.quote: You can use concurrent connections to Amazon S3 to fetch different byte ranges from within the same object. This helps you achieve higher aggregate throughput versus a single whole-object request. Fetching smaller ranges of a large object also allows your application to improve retry times when requests are interrupted.

question: What can an S3 Lifecycle configuration do to objects?

transition objects to less expensive storage classes

values.display: stop incomplete multipart uploads
remove expired object delete markers

question: Does a Lifecycle expiration rule clean up incomplete multipart uploads?

values.display: don't remove incomplete multipart uploads
AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload

evidence.quote: Object expiration lifecycle configurations don't remove incomplete multipart uploads. To remove incomplete multipart uploads, you must use the `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` Lifecycle configuration action that's described later in this section.

claim: Each Lifecycle rule has a rule ID and a status (enabled or disabled); S3 performs no action of a disabled rule.
question: What happens to the actions of a Lifecycle rule whose status is disabled?

values.display: doesn't perform any actions specified in the rule

evidence.quote: Rule metadata that includes a rule ID, and a status that indicates whether the rule is enabled or disabled. If a rule is disabled, Amazon S3 doesn't perform any actions specified in the rule.

claim: A Lifecycle rule can filter objects by key prefix, object tags or both; combined filters use a logical AND, and one filter can have only one prefix and zero or more tags.
question: How can a Lifecycle rule select the objects it applies to?

values.display: key prefix, object tags, or a combination
only one prefix, and zero or more tags

evidence.quote: You can filter objects by key prefix, object tags, or a combination of both (in which case Amazon S3 uses a logical `AND` to combine the filters).

Amazon S3 combines these filters by using a logical `AND`. That is, the rule applies to the subset of objects with the specified key prefix and the specified tags. A filter can have only one prefix, and zero or more tags.

claim: When Lifecycle rules overlap, S3 Lifecycle optimizes for cost: of two overlapping expirations the shorter one is honored, and of two overlapping transitions the lower-cost storage class is chosen.
question: When two Lifecycle rules overlap, which expiration and which transition does S3 apply?

values.display: the shorter expiration policy is honored
the lower-cost storage class
optimizes for cost

evidence.quote: Generally, Amazon S3 Lifecycle optimizes for cost. For example, if two expiration policies overlap, the shorter expiration policy is honored so that data is not stored for longer than expected. Likewise, if two transition policies overlap, S3 Lifecycle transitions your objects to the lower-cost storage class.

claim: An exception to the cheapest-path rule: S3 Lifecycle favors S3 Intelligent-Tiering over any storage class except S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
question: In a Lifecycle conflict, which storage class is favored over the cheapest choice?

values.display: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is favored by S3 Lifecycle

evidence.quote: An exception to this general rule is with the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. S3 Intelligent-Tiering is favored by S3 Lifecycle over any storage class, aside from the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage classes.

claim: When an object is eligible for several Lifecycle actions on the same day, permanent deletion takes precedence over transition, and an S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval transition wins over an S3 Standard-IA or One Zone-IA transition.
question: If an object qualifies for expiration and transition on the same day, which happens?

values.display: Permanent deletion takes precedence over transition
chooses the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval transition

evidence.quote: Permanent deletion takes precedence over transition.
When an object is eligible for both an S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and an S3 Standard-IA (or an S3 One Zone-IA) transition, Amazon S3 chooses the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval transition.

claim: An object is eligible for only one S3 Lifecycle action per day; when multiple rules match, S3 applies the least costly action.
question: How many Lifecycle actions can apply to one object on one day, and which one is chosen?

values.display: only one S3 Lifecycle action per day
applies the least costly action

evidence.quote: An object is eligible for only one S3 Lifecycle action per day. When multiple rules match, Amazon S3 applies the least costly action.

claim: In a versioning-enabled bucket, a Lifecycle expiration does not permanently delete data: if the current version is not a delete marker, S3 adds a delete marker that becomes the current version, and the old current version becomes noncurrent. Expiration acts only on the current version.
question: What does a Lifecycle expiration do in a versioning-enabled bucket?

values.display: adds a delete marker with a unique version ID
applies only to an object's current version

evidence.quote: If the current object version is not a delete marker, Amazon S3 adds a delete marker with a unique version ID. This makes the current version noncurrent, and the delete marker the current version.
Object expiration applies only to an object's current version (it has no impact on noncurrent object versions).

claim: S3 makes all expired objects unavailable; whether they are permanently removed depends on the versioning state of the bucket.
question: Does a Lifecycle expiration always permanently remove the object?

values.display: makes all expired objects unavailable
depends on the versioning state of the bucket

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 makes all expired objects unavailable. Whether the objects are permanently removed depends on the versioning state of the bucket.

claim: The NoncurrentVersionExpiration action permanently deletes noncurrent object versions, which cannot be recovered; it can be based on the number of days since the versions became noncurrent.
question: How do you make Lifecycle permanently delete old versions in a versioned bucket?

values.display: permanently delete noncurrent versions of objects
These deleted objects can't be recovered

evidence.quote: You can use the `NoncurrentVersionExpiration` action element to direct Amazon S3 to permanently delete noncurrent versions of objects. These deleted objects can't be recovered. You can base this expiration on a certain number of days since the objects became noncurrent.

claim: The Lifecycle Expiration action can also remove expired object delete markers (delete markers with no remaining object versions).
question: Can Lifecycle clean up delete markers that no longer have object versions?

values.display: remove any expired object delete markers

evidence.quote: You can also use the `Expiration` action to direct Amazon S3 to remove any expired object delete markers.

claim: A date-based Lifecycle action is not applied only once: S3 keeps applying it after the date has passed, for as long as the rule status is Enabled.
question: Is a date-based Lifecycle action applied once, or does it keep applying to new objects?

values.display: not a one-time action
as long as the rule status is

evidence.quote: The date-based action is not a one-time action. Amazon S3 continues to apply the date-based action even after the date has passed, as long as the rule status is `Enabled`.

claim: For a days-based Lifecycle action, S3 adds the days in the rule to the object creation time and rounds the result up to the next day at midnight UTC.
question: How does S3 compute the date of a days-based Lifecycle action?

values.display: rounding up the resulting time to the next day at midnight UTC

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 calculates the time by adding the number of days specified in the rule to the object creation time and rounding up the resulting time to the next day at midnight UTC.

claim: If S3 moves or expires an object later than it became eligible, billing changes apply as soon as the object becomes eligible; the exception is a transition to S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which is billed at the new class only after the transition.
question: When does billing change after a Lifecycle rule makes an object eligible for transition or expiration?

values.display: as soon as the object becomes eligible
billing changes don't occur until the object has transitioned

evidence.quote: If there is any delay between when an object becomes eligible for a lifecycle action and when Amazon S3 transfers or expires your object, billing changes are applied as soon as the object becomes eligible for the lifecycle action.

The one exception to this behavior is if you have a lifecycle rule to transition to the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. In that case, billing changes don't occur until the object has transitioned to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

claim: S3 may remove an object some time after its expiration date, but you are not charged for expiration or for the storage time of an expired object.
question: Do you pay for storage of an object between its Lifecycle expiration date and its actual removal?

values.display: not charged for expiration or the storage time

evidence.quote: There may be a delay between the expiration date and the date at which Amazon S3 removes an object. You are not charged for expiration or the storage time associated with an object that has expired.
